facts.statement: The only known specimen is a nearly complete frontoparietal dome belonging to a subadult individual.
facts.quote: Amtocephale is known from the holotype MPC-D 100/1203, a nearly complete frontoparietal dome of a subadult individual.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2011 by Mahito Watabe, Khishigjaw Tsogtbaatar, and Robert M. Sullivan.
facts.quote: Amtocephale was first named by Mahito Watabe, Khishigjaw Tsogtbaatar and Robert M. Sullivan in 2011

facts.statement: This dinosaur lived during the early Late Cretaceous in the southern Gobi Desert of Mongolia.
facts.quote: Amtocephale is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from early Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian-Coniacian stages) deposits of southern Gobi Desert, Mongolia.

facts.statement: The fossil site at Amtgai was excavated in 1993, 1994, 2001, and 2004.
facts.quote: The Amtgai locality, an outcrop of fossil beds within small cliffs, was excavated in 1993, 1994, 2001 and 2004.

facts.statement: Recent dating suggests the formation containing the fossils is between 95.9 and 89.6 million years old.
facts.quote: Recent calcite U–Pb measurements performed by Kurumada and colleagues in 2020 have estimated the age of the Baynshire Formation between 95.9 ± 6.0 Ma and 89.6 ± 4.0 Ma

facts.statement: Based on its age, Amtocephale is considered the oldest known pachycephalosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: which supports Amtocephale as the oldest known pachycephalosaurid.

facts.statement: The fused skull dome measured 53.2 mm in length and 19 mm in maximum thickness.
facts.quote: The frontoparietal dome, formed by a fusion of the frontals in front and the parietals in the back, has a length of 53.2 mm and a maximal thickness of 19 mm.

facts.statement: The parietal bones contributed an exceptionally large 41% of the total dome length.
facts.quote: The contribution to the dome length of the parietal part is exceptionally large, with a portion of 41%.

facts.statement: The species is classified within the family Pachycephalosauridae.
It lived approximately 85 million years ago during the Cenomanian and Santonian stages of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Superior durante el Cenomaniense y el Santoniense hace aproximadamente 85 millones de años, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for this genus spans from the Cenomanian to the Santonian stages (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Santonian (100.5 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Amtocephale is the oldest pachycephalosaurid, as this depends on the exact age of the geological formation.
facts.quote: Amtocephale was assigned to the Pachycephalosauridae and is perhaps the oldest pachycephalosaurid known, depending on the exact age of the formation.

rejected.statement: Amtocephale gobiensis is the only known species in the extinct genus Amtocephale.
